tasks.short: Prepare curriculum-aligned course objectives and outlines

steps.what: Prepare course objectives and outlines following current curriculum guidelines

loop.purpose: Draft wording and sequence for instructor-selected curriculum objectives
loop.input: Verified requirements, chosen objectives, learner context, course duration and approved resources
loop.output: Draft outline with each objective mapped to a supplied requirement
loop.check: Instructor verifies coverage, level, sequencing, assessability and that no requirement or learning outcome is invented
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; gaps or weak alignment are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native course templates are tried first; adapting wording and sequence to the selected curriculum needs contextual drafting

steps.what: Check curriculum alignment and approve the course objectives and outline

tasks.design: Use existing {LMS} structures and {DOCS} templates before a bounded loop proposes outline wording. The instructor chooses objectives, checks every curriculum link and approves the exact course outline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected requirements must be expressed as a coherent course sequence.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can propose a first outline without deciding curriculum obligations.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing coverage, learning progression and realistic course time.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor knows what learners need and whether the outline can be taught.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft wording, with curriculum decisions retained.

evidence.claim: Easygenerator turns source documents or slides into a first course draft; this supports drafting capability, not measured time savings for this instructor task.
Model knowledge: curriculum choices and final alignment checks remain human; the proposed saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is course objectives and outline preparation, excluding daily lesson plans and course-revision decisions in task 6844.

Within s1 the instructor captures curriculum version and requirement IDs, selected objectives, learner level, duration, prerequisites, assessment intentions and resource versions before drafting. The retained 52.5 hours include curriculum interpretation, capture and semantic correction; no free structured course brief is assumed.
Missing requirements or uncertain alignment return to manual preparation. Test native templates first; existing runtime earns no new saving.
Six extra focal hours count template changes, sample alignment audits and failed-draft handling; no additional coordinator review is transferred free.
unknowns: Applicable national and institution curriculum requirements
research_questions: Does drafting save time after curriculum interpretation and full alignment checking?

already_counted.description: Curriculum design, structured brief capture and draft checks
Final curriculum alignment and outline approval

incremental.description: Template changes, alignment audits and failed drafts

approvals.approved_version: Exact course outline, objectives, curriculum versions and source map checked in s2; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70*0.75+30=82.5; gross 17.5%, net 11.5% after 6 focal upkeep. Range covers failed drafts with zero gain through 11 points of wording removed minus 6 upkeep. Curriculum interpretation and final checking remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare administrative reports on students and activities

steps.what: Verify student and activity facts and select the required report fields
Prepare report tables and standard fields from verified student and activity records
Complete explanatory comments and check reports before release to administration

tasks.design: Configure native {LMS} report exports and {DOCS} templates to populate selected verified facts. The instructor writes explanatory comments, checks student identity and meaning, and approves the report for its authorised administrative recipient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and progress facts can be recopied into recurring administrative forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports and templates can reuse verified fields without assessing students anew.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining progress fairly and correcting incomplete records.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor understands context behind the recorded facts.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated copying with reporting judgement retained.

reach.task: Agree administrative report definitions and correction routes

evidence.claim: Momoyoga supports attendance reports and class records; this is adjacent native reporting capability rather than evidence of adult-education progress reporting accuracy or time savings.
Model knowledge: templates can copy verified administrative fields while instructor comments and checking remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is report preparation, excluding original attendance capture, grading and student assessment. Those upstream tasks retain their own labour and are counted once.

Existing attendance and assessment owners produce original records. In s1 the instructor verifies and captures student IDs, period, attendance counts, assessed result versions, activity IDs, requested fields, report template version and authorised recipient; all report-specific capture and reconciliation remains in 40%.
Missing or disputed results return to manual report preparation; no automatically inferred progress judgement is assumed. Three other-role hours count administrator field-mapping upkeep.
Test native LMS reports first; existing automatic reporting earns no new saving. Seven extra focal hours count template changes, report audits and unusual reconciliation.
unknowns: Report fields and existing native exports
research_questions: Does field reuse save time after checking identities, periods and explanatory comments?

already_counted.description: Fact checks and structured reporting capture
Explanatory comments and final report approval

incremental.description: Template changes, report audits and extra reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Exact report, student/result source versions, reporting period, comments and authorised recipient checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+25=65; gross 35%, net 28% after 7 focal upkeep. Range covers existing automatic reports with zero gain through 19 points of copying removed minus 7 upkeep. Fact checks and comments remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review instructional content, methods and student evaluations for strengths and weaknesses
Develop recommendations for course revision, development or elimination

tasks.design: The instructor reviews actual course evidence in {LMS} and {DOCS}, then recommends changes. No automated student score or generated comment summary replaces substantive course evaluation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course quality depends on evidence with different strengths and limitations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support review without proving that interpretation can be removed.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing course weaknesses from cohort, access or delivery effects.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor understands teaching context and the consequences of eliminating or revising a course.

reach.task: Compare course revisions with curriculum needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: substantive course review and recommendations remain human; a comment-summary preparation baseline is not assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is course review and recommendations, excluding later outline drafting in task 6841 and original evaluation collection.

Students and existing course-record owners supply evaluations and outcomes. The instructor checks them and produces findings in s1 before recommendations in s2; no free structured course-quality verdict is assumed.
Test native evaluation views first; existing runtime earns no saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new analysis tool is introduced.
unknowns: Evaluation coverage and course decision rights
research_questions: Which evidence supports a course change rather than merely reflecting cohort differences?

already_counted.description: Substantive course review and change recommendations

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+35=100; net 0%. Evidence interpretation and course recommendations retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Register, orient and assess new adult students

steps.what: Register new students after verifying required information
Orient new students to the course and relevant procedures
Assess new students according to current standards and procedures

tasks.design: The instructor verifies registration in {LMS}, orients students with material in {DOCS} and conducts the required assessment. No automatic admission, support-need or placement decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: New-student needs and information often require clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms support registration but no repeated-copy baseline is established here.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding prior learning, access needs and uncertain assessment responses.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor hears the student's circumstances and interprets assessment fairly.
tasks.altitude: Intake and assessment responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Intake standards and learner support boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: registration verification, orientation and new-student assessment remain human; existing form runtime is not a new labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is instructor intake, excluding original application production and later teaching.

Students supply registration information before s1, questions during s2 and assessment responses after the instructor administers assessment in s3. The instructor verifies information and interprets responses within the retained shares; no free learner-readiness score is assumed.
Test native intake forms first; existing runtime earns no labour saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no intake automation or extra student capture is introduced.
research_questions: Which intake information needs instructor clarification despite a completed form?

approvals.approved_version: Exact student assessment, response evidence, applicable standard version and support findings checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+35+40=100; net 0%. Intake conversation and assessment judgement remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Bounded outline drafts and native reports can reduce preparation while course judgement and student intake stay human.
reach: Coordinate curriculum alignment and source-record definitions with instructional staff.
role.ambitious_version: Traceable course preparation and reports with student and course decisions still owned by instructors.
